removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Proposition 10.1.9 at source lines 385-389: for any function f:A->B between sets, the relation ker(f,x,y) defined as f(x)=f(y) is effective. The author's proof (source lines 391-417) runs on the comparison map c_f(a) = (f(a), |a,refl|) into the image and on the kernel pair of that map. The two identifications that have to be carried out are not routine: the type c_f(x)=c_f(y) is first rewritten as a sum over p:f(x)=f(y) with a transported truncation on each side, and the collapse of that sum uses the fact that the fibre of f is a mere proposition; one then has to see that the resulting equivalence of kernel pairs is precisely effectivity. The statement records only the relation and the conclusion, and neither the comparison map nor the mere-proposition step appears in it.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.13 at source lines 537-540: if A is a mere proposition then its suspension is a set and A is equivalent to the path space north = south. The 71-line proof is an encode-decode argument that has to be built from scratch: it defines a family P on susp(A) x susp(A) with values unit and A (lines 543-554), checks that this definition survives the meridian, which is where an inhabitant of A is used to make A equivalent to unit and univalence turns the equivalence into the needed identity (lines 555-569), and checks mere-propositionality of every P(x,y) by double induction (lines 569-571). Sethood is then obtained from the author's criterion for reflexive mere relations, so the rest of the proof is the construction of tau : prd{x,y} P(x,y) -> (x = y) by double induction together with the two transport conditions along the meridian, the first of which needs function extensionality and the computation refl . merid(a) = merid(a) (lines 576-608). The statement records neither P nor the transport conditions.

removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file setmath.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 614-619 (book Theorem 10.1.14, Diaconescu theorem): the axiom of choice implies the law of excluded middle. The statement is a global implication between principles and gives no construction, and the proof (source lines 621-646) has to build the whole argument around one mere proposition A: the two-point map into the suspension of A has to be shown surjective, which needs a fibre over each pole and the fact that truncated fibres are mere propositions; choice then supplies a section merely, whose existence is used together with decidable equality of the booleans to produce a disjunction; and that disjunction has to be transported along the injectivity of the section and the identification of the equality of the two poles with A. Which form of choice is used, why the suspension of a proposition is the right type, and where decidability enters are all invisible in the statement.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.3.7 at source lines 1009-1016: given a set B, a function g from the power set of B to B and a well-founded relation < on A, there is f:A->B with f(a)=g(setof{ f(a') | a'<a }) for every a:A. The author's proof (source lines 1019-1029) is short but its whole content is a single careful recursion: one has to recurse on the accessibility witness rather than on the element of A, supplying at each step not only the values fbar(a',s(a')) but the witnesses s(a') for the predecessors, and only then discharge the accessibility hypothesis through the well-foundedness of < to obtain a genuine function on A. The statement records the recursion equation but neither the accessibility recursion nor the passage from fbar to f.

removed_items.title: Assuming excluded middle, a relation is well-founded exactly when every nonempty subset merely has a minimal element
removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file setmath.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 1037-1040: under excluded middle, a relation is well-founded exactly when every nonempty subset merely has a minimal element. The proof (source lines 1041-1057) is carried out in full in both directions and its substance is not visible in the statement: the first direction introduces an auxiliary claim that no accessible element lies in a subset with no minimal element and establishes it by induction on the accessibility witness, using the merely existing smaller element together with access to the induction hypothesis at that element; the second direction forms the subset of non-accessible elements, applies the minimal-element hypothesis to it, and closes the argument by excluded middle together with induction on truncation, which is the step that turns mere accessibility into accessibility. Two directions, an auxiliary induction and a truncation induction are the substance of the card.

The author's proof (source lines 358-386) is a three-stage argument. The author's proof (source lines 662-670) is a short but genuinely dependent argument: two candidate preimages (a,f) and (a',f') are compared by forming inv(f') o f as an isomorphism between Fa and Fa' (lines 663-664), full faithfulness lifts it to an isomorphism g : a = a' with controlled action (line 665), and the hypothesis that A is a category is what converts that isomorphism into a path p whose transported image matches, after which the equality of the two sigma elements follows from the characterisation of equalities in dependent pair types (lines 666-667).
